newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Senate committee approves rainy day fund.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Senate committee approves rainy day fund.

text.p: Louisiana's Senate Finance Committee approved Thursday the creation of a budget stabilization trust fund that would be built with surplus general revenues and legislative allocations, a committee attorney said.
The proposal now goes to the full Senate, where it has wide support.
Technically, Louisiana already has a Revenue Stabilization and Mineral Trust Fund, but "It doesn't have any money in it," said Chris Crow, senior attorney for the Senate Finance Committee.

It was to have been funded in part with windfall revenues in excess of $750 million from the state's oil, gas and mineral royalties. But royalties have fallen short of that level and there was no money for the fund.
"We reached well over that during the OPEC years but only hit it once since the bottom fell out of oil," Crow said.
The new proposal keeps that potential revenue source, but also requires that the first $50 million or 25 percent of any budget surplus from nonrecurring revenues be put into the rainy day fund.
Louisiana has had year-end surplusses for several years, "so they're pretty sure we will have money for this fund," Crow said.

Legislators could also allocate additional nonrecurring revenues for the fund until it reaches a cap of four percent of total state revenue receipts for the previous fiscal year. That limit in 1998 would be $463 million.
Withdrawals from the fund would require two-thirds approval of the legislature.

Withdrawals up to one-third of the fund's value could be made if there is a projected deficit for the current year, or if the state's revenue estimating committee forecasts that revenues for the upcoming year will drop below those for the current year.
There is also a "super limit" that would prevent the expenditure of more than one-third of the fund even if both current and next-year deficits are projected.
"The sum of those can't exceed one-third of what you started with," Crow said.
Gov. Mike Foster and Treasurer Ken Duncan have urged the state to create a budget stabilization fund in order to strengthen Louisiana's credit rating.
